cross_insight: The energy sector is entering an era of structural tightness and de-globalization, where resource-rich states are weaponizing chokepoints like the Hormuz Strait. Even if physical conflicts cease, the extensive infrastructure damage to Middle Eastern oil and gas facilities, coupled with rising marine insurance rates, will prevent oil prices from returning to pre-war levels. In response, global powers are racing to secure alternative energy architectures; Japan is investing 100 trillion Yen into US-led SMR (Small Modular Reactor) partnerships, while trading houses like POSCO International are transforming into energy orchestrators by acquiring direct stakes in Australian gas (Senex Energy) and securing international food supply chains.
divergence: There is a division between those who view SMRs and nuclear power as an immediate, investable solution to the AI power bottleneck, and those who emphasize the long lead times, massive CapEx, and the competitive threat Japanese-backed SMR consortia pose to established heavy industries like Doosan Enerbility.
key_themes: Permanent geopolitical risk premiums on oil, gas, and maritime logistics
Government-backed SMR standard wars (US-Japan alliance vs. Korea)
Transition of trading firms to resource ownership ('Orchestrators')
watch_list: POSCO International (Australian Senex Energy production & EV motor core sales)
